newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Settlers wound Palestinian, fire at reporters.
newsitem.headline: Settlers wound Palestinian, fire at reporters.

text.p: Jewish settlers shot and wounded a Palestinian youth in Gaza on Monday during a clash over land which Arabs said had recently been seized by settlers, witnesses said.
They said a Jew from the Gush Katif settlement block fired at least three shots at three Palestinian journalists who arrived to cover a demonstration by Arab landowners.

"I shouted to the settler in Hebrew that we were reporters, but he cursed at us and continued to fire his pistol. One bullet barely missed us," a Reuters reporter said, describing the gunman as a middle-aged settler with a grey beard.
A settler spokesman said he knew of no such incident.
Israeli soldiers later arrived at the scene, punched a cameraman and kicked others, journalists said. One youth was shot in the knee and was taken to hospital.
"They broke into our farming village...and started destroying property. Our residents kicked them out and now the army has arrived," said Gush Katif settler spokesman Shlomo Kostiner.
"I know of no shots fired by settlers and no Palestinians who were wounded," he told Reuters.
The protest occurred against a backdrop of increased Israeli-Palestinian tension over the Israel's expansion of Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Palestinians said the protest began as settlers ploughed through Arab-owned land with a bulldozer. Sami Abu Salim, mayor of the PLO-ruled town of Deir al-Balah, said the land belonged to the Palestinian al-Abadleh family.
"They wanted to annex the land to the Gush Katif settlement," Abu Salim told Reuters.
